statement: Linear-cooling SA (T proportional to remaining time fraction, T0=3.0, 0.10s per restart) outperforms geometric-cooling SA (T*=0.9995) by ~1 point on Max-Cut (87.5 vs 86.6), because geometric cooling exhausts useful exploration in ~0.5ms while linear cooling uses the full restart budget.
regime: Max-Cut with n<=1000, m<=20000, 1s time limit, greedy+SA+restarts framework
mechanism: Geometric cooling (0.9995^k) drops temperature below 0.01 after ~10.6k iterations (~0.5ms), making the remaining ~0.4ms per restart equivalent to greedy. Linear cooling (T = T0*(1-t/budget)) ensures temperature scales from T0 to Tf across the full 0.10s SA phase, giving ~1.7M SA iterations of productive exploration per restart. Fewer but deeper restarts (9 vs 1000+) yield higher-quality cuts.
applicability_bounds: Tested on competition-style Max-Cut instances. The optimal restart budget (0.10s) may differ on larger/denser graphs or different hardware speeds.

statement: Linear-cooling SA with time-proportional restarts reduces RNG-seed variance from ~5 points (iter-1 FM+SA) to ~0.05 points (std 0.03), likely because the fixed 0.10s SA budget per restart is more deterministic than time-checked geometric cooling that races against the clock.
mechanism: The batched time check (every 256 iterations) and fixed SA budget per restart make each restart's behavior more predictable across seeds. Geometric cooling with per-iteration time checks introduces more timing-dependent variance.
applicability_bounds: Variance reduction observed on local hardware. Judge hardware variance may differ.
